questions.question: Who among the following Governor Generals enacted the law against the Sati practice in December 1829?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Lord William Bentinck**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lord William Bentinck (1828-1835)

 
 
• ​​During his tenure as Governor- General following were the various events that took place:
 
• Abolition of Sati and other cruel rites (1829).
 
• Suppression of thugs (1830).
 
• Charter Act of 1833.
 
• Resolution of 1835, and educational reforms and introduction of English as the official language.
 
• Annexation of Mysore (1831), Coorg (1834), and Central Cachar (1834).
 
• Treaty of 'perpetual friendship with Ranjeet Singh.
 
• Abolished the provincial court of appeal and circuit.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Canning**

 
 
• He was an English statesman and Governor-General of India during the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
 
• He was the Governor-General of India from 1856 - 1858 and viceroy from 1858 - 1862.
 
• He was the first Viceroy of India after the transfer of power from the East India Company to the Crown of Queen Victoria in 1858.
 
• After the rebellion, he presided over a smooth transfer and reorganization of government from the East India Company to the crown.
 
• He is credited with establishing the first three modern Universities in India, the University of Calcutta, the University of Madras, and the University of Bombay based on Wood's despatch.
 
• Canning also passed the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, of 1856 which was drafted by his predecessor Lord Dalhousie before the rebellion.​​​
 
 
 
• Lord Dalhousie:
 
 
• James Andrew Brown-Ramsay also known as Lord Dalhousie.
 
• He served as governor-general of India from 1848-1856.
 
• James Outram was made the British Resident of Awadh in place of Sleeman.
 
• He said that the administration of Awadh is very corrupt and the condition of the people is very contemplative.
 
• Outram's report was the basis for the annexation of Awadh.
 
• Lord Dalhousie annexed the Nawab of Awadh, Wajid Ali Shah on February 13, 1856, accusing him of misrule.
 
• Apart from Awadh, under the principle of Doctrine of Lapse, the merged territories- Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853), Nagpur (1854), and Karauli (1855).
 
• The first attempt towards railway construction in India was made by Lord Dalhousie in 1853 AD.
 
• It was laid between Bombay to Thane at the time of Dalhousie.
 
• The last expansion of British Indian territory took place during Dalhousie.
 
• During his tenure, for the first time, a separate public Works Department was created.
 
 
 
• **Lord Warren Hastings**
 
 
• In 1781, Warren Hastings, the first Governor-General of Bengal, established a madrasa in Calcutta for the study and teaching of Muslim law.
 
• Calcutta Madrasa, The (later Calcutta Aliya Madrasa) was the earliest of the state-managed educational institutions under British rule in India.
 
• Founded by Governor-General Warren Hastings in October 1780 with its entire expense borne by him for a year and a half, of course fully reimbursed later, the Bengal Government took it over in April 1782.
 
• Originally situated at Baithakkhana near Sealdah in Calcutta.
 
• It was shifted to its present site at Wellesley Square in 1827.
 
 

6d:T26bd

questions.question: Who amongst the following became the president of the second session of the Indian National Congress held in Calcutta in December 1886?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Nauroji**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Nauroji** became the president of the second session of the Indian National Congress held in Calcutta in December 1886.
 
• He is also known as the "Grand Old Man of India" and was one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Dadabhai Nauroji was a prominent Indian political leader, merchant, scholar, and writer who played a significant role in the early stages of the Indian independence movement.
 
• His presidency of the Indian National Congress marked a crucial step in the organization’s efforts to bring together various Indian leaders to push for political reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)** was founded in 1885 and played a pivotal role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• The first session of the INC was held in Bombay (now Mumbai) in December 1885, presided over by Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee.
 
• The INC aimed to create a platform for civic and political dialogue among educated Indians and to seek greater involvement of Indians in the governance of their country.
 
• Dadabhai Nauroji's efforts in economic analysis and his work in highlighting the drain of wealth from India to Britain were crucial in raising awareness about the economic exploitation of India under British rule.
 
• He was the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament, where he worked to influence British policy towards India.

questions.question: Vallabhbhai Patel and ________ helped Gandhi in Kheda by organising his tour of the villages and urging the peasants to stand firm against the government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indulal Yajnik**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vallabhbhai Patel and Indulal Yagnik helped Gandhi in Kheda by organizing his tour of the villages and urging the peasants to stand firm against the government.**
 
• **Vallabhbhai Patel**:
 
 
• A prominent figure in the Indian independence movement, Patel played a crucial role in mobilizing the peasants of Kheda and guiding them through the non-violent resistance movement.
 
• He was instrumental in organizing Gandhi's tour of the affected villages and persuading the farmers to withhold tax payments until the government granted relief. 
 
 
 
• **Indulal Yagnik:**
 
 
• A close associate of Gandhi, Yagnik was a dedicated social worker and journalist who actively participated in the Kheda Satyagraha.
 
• He accompanied Gandhi on his village tours and helped him connect with the local populace. Yagnik's persuasive skills and unwavering commitment to the cause were instrumental in galvanizing the peasants' resolve.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jamnalal Bajaj:-**

 
 
• He was an Indian industrialist, philanthropist, and freedom fighter.
 
• He was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi and actively participated in the Indian independence movement.
 
• Bajaj was known for his commitment to Gandhian principles of non-violence, simplicity, and social reform.
 
• He founded the Bajaj Group, a conglomerate with interests in various industries, and also established educational and social institutions to uplift society.
 
 
 
• **Mohammad Ali Jinnah:-**
 
 
• He was a key political leader in the Indian subcontinent during the British colonial era.
 
• He became the leader of the All-India Muslim League and played a pivotal role in the creation of Pakistan in 1947, advocating for a separate Muslim-majority nation.
 
• Jinnah was a skilled lawyer and an advocate for Muslim rights in the Indian political landscape, eventually becoming the first Governor-General of Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Motilal Nehru:-**
 
 
• He was a prominent figure in India's struggle for independence and the father of Jawaharlal Nehru, who later became the first Prime Minister of India.
 
• Motilal was a successful lawyer and a leader in the Indian National Congress.
 
• He was known for his efforts in shaping the Congress party and for his role in the Nehru Report of 1928, which proposed constitutional reforms for India.
 
• Motilal Nehru was a key figure in the political landscape of pre-independence India.

questions.question: The Arms Act was passed in _____ that prevented Indians from keeping arms without an appropriate license.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**1878**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Arms Act**

 
 
• Between 1876 and 1880, Lord Lytton held the position of Viceroy of India.
 
• He approved both the 1878** Arms Act** and the Vernacular Press** Act.**
 
• The** Arms** Act was developed by the British during the 19th century in response to the rising Indian nationalism.
 
• It became law in 1878.
 
• The production and sale of fir**earms** in the nation were controlled by this statute.
 
• No Indian was permitted to produce, market, or even possess a weapon without first obtaining a government permission.
 
• The British intended to prevent Indians from possessing rifles and pistols because they did not want another uprising like the one that occurred in 1857 CE.
 
• The act underwent significant amendments in **1959 and 1983**, but there was no specific amendment that disallowed Indians from possessing arms.
 
• However, in **1962**, the Indian government passed the Defence of India Rules, which prohibited the possession of arms and ammunition by any person without a valid license.
 
• **This law was enacted during the Indo-China** War to prevent unauthorized persons from possessing arms that could be used against the country's interests.
 
• In **1983**, the Arms Act was amended to further regulate the **possession of firearms and ammunition in the country**.
 
• The amendment tightened the licensing requirements and imposed stricter penalties for** violations of the law.****​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Litton****​**

 
 
• Edward Robert Lytton Bulwer-Lytton, 1st Earl of Lytton, also known as Lord Lytton, was an English politician who was Viceroy of India from 1876 to 1880.
 
• The first Famine Commission was set up in 1878 under the Chairmanship of Sir Richard Strachey. The commission recommended state interference in food trade in the event of famine. India witnessed another major famine in 1896-97.
 
• Lytton's viceroyalty was characterized by ruthlessness in both domestic and foreign affairs.
 
• At the time, India was in the grip of a famine caused by crop failure in 1876. In response, he called a **Durbar and declared Queen Victoria to be the "Empress of India".**
 
• Vernacular Press Act**(1878**)​
 
 
• People were dissatisfied with Lytton's unpopular policies, and the native vernacular press mocked him. He drafted the Vernacular Press Act to curtail the wings of the Vernacular Press.
 
• By virtue of this act, District Magistrates were empowered, without prior permission from the government, to compel a printer and publisher of any kind to enter into a bond, undertaking not to publish anything that might incite discontent against the government.
 
• The magistrate was also given the authority to deposit security, which could be confiscated if the printer violated the bond.
 
• If the printer violates this again, his press may be seized.
 
• The worst aspect of this Act was that it discriminated against Native Vernacular Press and loyal Anglo-Indian Press and was dubbed the Gagging Act.
 
• It was specifically aimed at Amrita Bazaar Patrika, which had turned English overnight in order to avoid being caught up in the act.
 
 
 
 

9d:T

questions.question: When did the second urbanisation in Ganga Valley take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6th Century BCE**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The second urbanisation in the Ganga Valley took place during the **6th Century BCE**.
 
• This period marked the rise of large cities and the establishment of powerful kingdoms and republics in the region.
 
• It was characterized by significant advancements in trade, economy, and culture.
 
• The period saw the emergence of important cities such as Varanasi, Pataliputra, and Rajagriha.
 
• It also witnessed the rise of major religious movements including Buddhism and Jainism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first urbanisation in the Indian subcontinent is associated with the Indus Valley Civilization, which flourished around 2500 BCE.
 
• The second urbanisation period is noted for the development of the Mahajanapadas, which were large territorial states.
 
• Key factors contributing to this urbanisation included the use of iron tools and weapons, which facilitated agricultural expansion and military conquests.
 
• The period also saw the compilation of significant literary works such as the Upanishads and other early Buddhist texts.

questions.question: Who was/were the founder(s) of the Theosophical Society?

options.text: H P Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott
Charles W Leadbeater and Emily Lutyens

questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **H P Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Theosophical Society **was formally established on November 17, 1875.
 
• In New York City, New York, by** Helena Petrovna Blavatsky, Colonel Henry Steel Olcott, William Quan Judge**, and other individuals.
 
• In a few years, Olcott and Blavatsky established the International Headquarters at Adyar in Madras (currently Chennai).
 
• They did so because they thought that spreading the theosophical movement in India was a good idea.
 
• **Theosophical society played a significant role in the Indian Renaissance.**
 
• It emphasized the depth of Indian religious concepts in the Western world.
 
• It brought back to life a number of philosophical, occult, religious, and other texts.
 
• India’s political and social awakening was greatly aided by its contributions to women’s empowerment and education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Madam Bhikaji Cama - **

 
 
• Bhikaji Rustom Cama, also known as Madam Cama, was a stalwart of the Indian freedom struggle. 
 
• She was born on September 24, 1861, to Sorabji Framji Patel and Jaijibai Sorabai Patel. 
 
• She penned, published, and distributed revolutionary works such as ‘Bande Mataram’ and ‘Madan’s Talwar’. 
 
• She was an active member of the Indian freedom movement.
 
• She propagated the cause of Swaraj among the Indian community in England. In 1907, Madam Cama became the first person to hoist the Indian flag in Germany. 
 
• The flag was designed by Bhikaiji Cama and fellow activist Vinayak Damodar Savarkar. 
 
• Bhikaiji Cama moved to Paris where she founded the Paris Indian Society. Munchershah Burjorji Godrej and S.R. Rana were the co-founders of this society.
 
 
 
• **Annie Besant -**
 
 
• She became head of the Theosophy Society, and later on, in 1916,
 
• She established the Indian Home Rule League and also became the president of India's National Congress.

questions.question: Which of the following is an autobiography of a Bengali illiterate woman who secretly acquired literacy skills to read sacred texts in an age when girls and women were denied education and deemed fit only for household chores?

questions.question: The deliberations of the representatives at the Third Round Table Conference was held during the later months of which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1932**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Third Round Table Conference:-**

 
 
• **It was a series of meetings held in London from November 17, 1932, to December 24, 1932, to discuss the future of British India.**
 
• The conference was attended by representatives of the British government, Indian princes, and various political parties, including the Indian National Congress (INC).
 
• However, the INC, led by Mahatma Gandhi, ultimately boycotted the conference due to disagreements with the British government over the scope of reforms and the representation of minority groups.
 
• Despite the absence of the INC, the Third Round Table Conference made some significant progress towards Indian self-government.
 
• The conference agreed to establish a federal system of government for India, with a central government and provincial legislatures.
 
• **It also agreed to expand the franchise and introduce measures to protect minority groups.**
 
• However, the conference failed to reach an agreement on the composition of the central legislature, which remained a major stumbling block to further constitutional reforms. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Round Table Conference:-**

 
 
• **The First Round Table Conference was held in London in three sessions between November 1930 and January 1931.**
 
• The conference was attended by representatives of the British government, Indian princes, and various political parties, but the Indian National Congress (INC) did not participate.
 
• The conference discussed a range of issues related to the future of British India, including dominion status, provincial autonomy, and minority rights.
 
• The conference did not reach any major agreements, but it did help to establish a framework for further discussions.
 
 
 
• **Second Round Table Conference:-**
 
 
• **The Second Round Table Conference was held in London in two sessions between September and December 1931.**
 
• The conference was attended by representatives of the British government, Indian princes, and various political parties, including the INC.
 
• The INC participated in the conference after the British government agreed to release Gandhi from prison and suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement.
 
• The conference discussed a range of issues related to the future of British India, including dominion status, provincial autonomy, and minority rights.
 
• The conference reached some agreements on these issues, but it did not resolve all of the outstanding issues.

questions.question: In which year did the annexation of Awadh by Lord Dalhousie take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1856**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The annexation of Awadh by Lord Dalhousie took place in the year **1856**.
 
• Lord Dalhousie was the Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856.
 
• The annexation was justified by Dalhousie under the pretext of misgovernment by the Nawab of Awadh.
 
• This event was one of the significant causes leading to the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
 
• The policy of annexation was part of Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse, which aimed at expanding British territories in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Dalhousie** is often criticized for his aggressive policies of annexation.
 
• His tenure saw the annexation of several other states including Punjab, Jhansi, and Nagpur.
 
• The Doctrine of Lapse allowed the British to annex any princely state where the ruler did not have a direct heir.
 
• The annexation of Awadh was particularly controversial and led to widespread resentment among the local population.
 
• This resentment contributed to the widespread support for the 1857 rebellion, also known as the First War of Indian Independence.

questions.question: Who wrote the patriotic song ‘Sare Jahan Se Achha Hindustan Hamara’ that was published in the weekly journal Ittehad on 16 August 1904?

• Iqbal's vision of an independent state for Muslims in north-western India was to inspire the creation of Pakistan.
 
• His notable works include **“Asrar-e-Khudi”** and **“Bang-e-Dra”**.

questions.question: Who among the following had written the novel Coolie, that concentrated on social misery caused by inhumanity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mulk Raj Anand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mulk Raj Anand **authored the novel **"Coolie," first published** in **1936**, which serves as a **critique of British rule in India and the caste system.**
 
• The narrative centers around Munoo, a **14-year-old boy, **depicting the hardships and exploitation he endures as a result of societal and political constructs.
 
• Anand's work is renowned for its realistic and compassionate portrayal of the impoverished in India. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mulk Raj Anand **was an esteemed Indian writer who wrote primarily in English, renowned for his portrayal of the lives of the marginalized castes in traditional Indian society.
 
• As one of the pioneers of** Indo-Anglian fiction**, alongside R. K. Narayan, Ahmad Ali, and Raja Rao, he was among the first writers based in India to garner international recognition.
 
• Anand gained acclaim for his protest novel **"Untouchable" (1935),** followed by other notable works focusing on the struggles of the Indian poor, such as "Coolie" (1936) and "Two Leaves and a Bud" (1937).
 
• Anand was honored with the civilian award of the Padma Bhushan for his contributions to literature.

questions.question: The claim for ‘swarajya’ or self-government within the British Empire, on the model of self-governing colonies like Australia and Canada, was put forward from the Congress platform in 1906 by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The claim for **"swarajya" or self-government** within the British Empire, on the model of self-governing colonies like Australia and Canada, was put forward from the Congress platform in the **Calcutta session of 1906.**
 
• The session was presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji, who is considered the **"Grand Old Man of India" **for his contributions to the Indian independence movement. 
 
• In his presidential address, Naoroji called for **"self-government or swaraj like the United Kingdom or the colonies"** of Australia or Canada. 
 
• This was a significant shift in the Congress's position, as it had previously been more focused on seeking limited reforms within the British Raj.
 
• The Calcutta session's resolution on swaraj was a compromise between the **"moderates" and "extremists"** within the Congress. 
 
• The **moderates, led by Gopal Krishna Gokhale**, wanted to pursue a gradual path to self-government, while the extremists, led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, wanted to demand complete independence. 
 
• The resolution on swaraj represented a middle ground, calling for self-government within the British Empire, but with a degree of autonomy that would be similar to that of self-governing colonies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai:**

 
 
• He was an** Indian author, politician, and freedom warrior.**
 
• He was commonly referred to as **Punjab Kesari.**
 
• He was one of the **Lal Bal Pal trimurti's three members. **
 
 
 
• **Bipin Chandra Pal:**
 
 
• He was a member of the** trio known as "Lal Bal Pal."**
 
• Along with** Sri Aurobindo**, Pal was one of the primary designers of the **Swadeshi movement.**

questions.question: The Anushilan Samiti was active in which part of the Indian subcontinent in the 20th century?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Anushilan Samiti:

 
 
• **The Anushilan Samiti** was founded by Pramathanath Mitra and includes Jatindranath Banerjee, Barindra Kumar Ghosh and others.
 
• In April 1906, an inner circle within Anushilan (Barindra Kumar Ghosh, Bhupendranath Dutta) started the weekly Yugantar and conducted a few abortive ‘actions’.
 
• In 1907, an abortive attempt was made by the Yugantar group on the life of a very unpopular British official, Sir Fuller
 
• Anushilan group was arrested including the Ghosh brothers, Aurobindo and Barindra, who were tried in the Alipore conspiracy case, variously called Manicktolla bomb conspiracy or Muraripukur conspiracy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pramathanath Mitra founded the Anushilan Samiti on March 24, 1902.
 
• It had two branches:
 
 
• the Jugantar Group in Calcutta
 
• the Dhaka Anushilan Samiti in Dhaka.
 
 
 
• The Samiti published "Bhavani Mandir" in 1905.
 
• They advocated military training in their 1907 publication, "Vartaman Rananiti."
 
• As a division of Anushilan Samiti, Dhaka Anushilan Samiti was established in November 1905. Pulin Bihar Das served as its leader when it was established.
 
• After Pulin Das was detained in the Barisal Conspiracy case in 1913, the development of this samiti was put on hold.
 
• Additionally, it should be noted that Dhaka Anushilan Samiti did not take part in the German World War I plot.
 
• Anushilan Samiti was an Indian health club that anti-British revolutionaries utilised as a covert organisation.
 
• In the early half of the 20th century, it encouraged the use of revolutionary violence to overthrow the British in India.
 
• In Bengal, in 1902, a combination of neighbourhood gyms and youth organisations came together to form the organisation.
 
• It had two significant, albeit independent, branches in East and West Bengal: the Jugantar group and Dhaka Anushilan Samiti, which was based in Dhaka (centred in Calcutta).

questions.question: Who among the following repealed the Vernacular Press Act of 1878?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Ripon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​Lord Ripon (1880-1884)__:

 __
 
• Lord Rippon repealed the Vernacular Press Act of 1878.
 
• First Factory Act was passed during the administration of Lord Ripon (1880-1884).
 
• First Factory Act was passed in the year 1881.
 
• According to the Act, Children under seven years old should not be employed by factories and reduced working hours for children.
 
• It mandated that dangerous machines should be properly fenced to prevent any untoward incident.
 
• In Lord Ripon's tenure, Local self-Government resolution was passed.
 
• It was not an Act but a resolution by the government in the year 1882.
 
• The Financial liberalization that started under Lord Mayo (1869-1872) was continued by Lord Ripon.
 
• The resolution helped to establish Local Boards with non-Official members at the provincial level and it was the basis of modern-day municipalities in this country.
 
• Lord Ripon was appointed as Viceroy of India in 1880.
 
• Lord Ripon was the son of Prime Minister F.J.Robinson(UK).
 
• The Factory Act: The first factory was passed by Lord Ripon. The act prohibited the working of children below seven years and a limited number of working hours for children below 12 years.
 
• Lord Ripon appointed an education commissioner under the chairmanship of Sir William Hunter.
 
• He also increased age requirement for civil services from 18 years to 21 years which were reduced by Lord Lytton (1876-1880) from 21 years to 18 years.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Northbrook**

 
 
• The Indian Christian Marriage Act of 1872 also called the Native Marriage Act
 
• It was enacted during the viceroyalty of Lord Northbrook (1872-1876).
 
 
 
• Lord Lytton
 
 
• ​The Vernacular Press Act was passed in 1878 by Viceroy Lord Lytton (1876-1880).
 
• This Act allowed Magistrate to collect security deposits from Regional Language/Native language/Vernacular newspapers and confiscate their printing press if they published anything against the crown.
 
• However, these same rules are not applied to English Language Printing Press.
 
 
 
• Lord Dufferin​ 
 
 
• He fought the Third Anglo-Burmese War (1885-86).
 
• The formation of INC took place during his tenure in 1885.

questions.question: In which year did Lord Dalhousie introduce the railway line in British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1853**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1853** is the year when Lord Dalhousie introduced the railway line in British India.
 
• The first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853, from Bombay (now Mumbai) to Thane, covering a distance of 34 km (21 miles).
 
• This event marked the beginning of the railway system in India, which played a crucial role in the country's economic and social development.
 
• Lord Dalhousie's tenure as the Governor-General of India saw significant infrastructure development, including the introduction of railways, telegraphs, and postal services.
 
• The introduction of the railway system was a part of Dalhousie's larger plan to modernize India and integrate its markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Dalhousie** served as the Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856.
 
• He is often credited with laying the foundation of modern infrastructure in India.
 
• His policies, including the Doctrine of Lapse, had a significant impact on the political landscape of India.
 
• The railway network expanded rapidly in the following decades, becoming one of the largest in the world.
 
• The introduction of railways facilitated faster movement of goods and people, contributing to the economic integration of various regions of India.

questions.question: In which of the following years, were separate electorates introduced in the Imperial Legislative Assembly elections in the name of Morley- Minto Reforms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Council Act, 1909**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Council Act, 1909**, also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms, introduced separate electorates for Muslims for the first time.
 
• This act allowed the election of Indian members to the various legislative councils in India, both at the central and provincial levels.
 
• It marked a significant step in the political representation of Indians under British rule.
 
• The separate electorates meant that Muslims could elect their representatives separately, which was intended to address the concerns of the Muslim community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Morley-Minto Reforms** were named after John Morley, the Secretary of State for India, and Lord Minto, the Viceroy of India.
 
• These reforms were seen as a response to the growing demand for greater Indian participation in governance.
 
• While the reforms did not meet all the demands of Indian nationalists, they were a crucial step towards the development of a representative government in India.
 
• The introduction of separate electorates was a contentious issue and had long-term implications for Indian politics, influencing future constitutional developments.

questions.question: The first President of the All India Trade Union Congress was ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Lala Lajpat Rai__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

All India Trade Union Congress:

__
 
• The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) is the oldest trade union federation in India.
 
• It is associated with the Communist Party of India.
 
• According to provisional statistics from the Ministry of Labour, AITUC had a membership of 14.2 million in 2013.
 
• It was founded on 31 October 1920 with Lala Lajpat Rai as its first president.
 
• Until 1945 when unions became organised on party lines, it was the primary trade union organisation in India.
 
• The main purpose of labour unions is to give workers the power to negotiate for more favourable working conditions and other benefits through collective bargaining.
 
• The following are the objectives of a trade union:
 
 
• To improve the economic lot of workers by securing them better wages.
 
• To secure workers better working conditions.
 
• To secure bonuses for the workers from the profits of the enterprise/organization.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **C Rajagopalachari**

 
 
• C. Rajagopalachari (1878-1972) was an Indian lawyer, writer and independence activist.
 
• He was popular as **Rajaji, C.R. and Mootharignar Rajaji.**
 
• He was the **last Governor-General **before India became a republic.
 
• He is remembered for his contribution to the independence struggle as well as his intellectual and administrative prowess.
 
• **In 1954, he was honoured with India’s highest civilian award, Bharat Ratna.**
 
 
 
• **Chandra Shekhar Azad**
 
 
• ​Azad was born on 23rd July 1906 in the Alirajpur district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• Chandra Shekhar, then a 15-year-old student, joined a Non-Cooperation Movement in December 1921. As a result, he was arrested.
 
• On being presented before a magistrate, he gave his name as "Azad" (The Free), his father's name as "Swatantrata" (Independence) and his residence as "Jail". Therefore, he came to be known as Chandra Shekhar Azad.
 
• After the suspension of the non-cooperation movement in 1922 by Gandhi, Azad joined Hindustan Republican Association (HRA).
 
• Most of the fund collection for revolutionary activities was done through robberies of government property. In line with the same, Kakori Train Robbery near Kakori, Lucknow was done in 1925 by HRA.
 
• He died at Azad Park in Allahabad on 27th February 1931.
 
 
 
• **Motilal Nehru**
 
 
• **​**Pandit Motilal Nehru was a lawyer and politician who was born in the year 1861.
 
• He was elected to United Provinces Council__ in 1909.
 
• He was contemporary of Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya.
 
• He attended the **Delhi Durbar in 1911 **in honour of the visit of King George V.
 
• Motilal was elected **President of the United Province Congress in the year 1911**.
